objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (19 November 2026) on JUNCTION-KINDS-20261119-001#1, bounded to three rules: in the ten break-shape eddies with W = y^2(1 + y), the junctions of each round pair one to one with ancestors two or three rounds back (a perfect matching of the spine relation). Does a rule read from the growth pick those partners: the newest ancestor, the ancestor reached by the most parent chains, or by the fewest? stop_rule: Stop at the verdicts on the three rules and the uniqueness readout.
title: Can the growth pick its own spine?
